Date: Sat, 15 Sep 2028 02:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call technical summary + artifacts (kernel contention confirmed)

Summary of triage performed overnight (details below and attached artifacts):

What we observed:
- Kernel-level contention in tokenizer memcpy on runtime build 2028.09.13-patch-2 causing spin locks; reproducible on two nodes in us-west-2b.
- KV cache miss rate increased ~18% when contention started; this caused additional latency amplification for tokenized requests.
- No evidence of network saturation or cloud provider throttling.

Actions taken:
1) Rolled back runtime to 2028.09.13-base on affected nodes (rollback completed 2028-09-14T09:50:00-07:00).
2) Re-routed traffic for Blue Harbor to us-west-2a warm standby (auto-failover executed).
3) Enabled no-cache fallback for the affected pool for 30m while we validate stability.
4) Kicked off a background job to rebuild KV cache entries for MH-4932 and MH-4990 priority namespaces.

Current status (as of 2028-09-15T02:00:00-07:00):
- 5xx rate back down to ~0.4% (from peak ~8%).
- Median tokenization latency reduced from ~520ms (peak) to ~120ms. Checkout retry queue draining; estimated 20 minutes to clear at current throughput.

Next steps and risks:
- We will perform a targeted canary of the patch only after we complete a micro-benchmarking pass against tokenizer memcpy permutations (ticket JIRA-RED-1489).
- Risk: reintroducing the patch without addressing kernel memcpy path may cause repeat regressions; recommend holding patch for the next stable rollout window.

Artifacts attached for Blue Harbor and internal review:
- telemetry_dump_0914.csv (sampled traces)
- kvcache_snapshot_0915.bin (kv cache snapshot)
- flamegraph_0915.svg (tokenizer hot path)

Grace Oconnor
SRE, Inference Platform
